title: Calabash Water Drum
summary: Water drums of the Sahel are made from half-gourds floated upside down in a basin or pot of water. Players strike the curved back with mallets or the hand, and the water around and under the gourd lends a deep, rounded boom; pressing or lifting the gourd bends the tone.
howToPlay: Four pads stand for the strokes: a deep one, a middle one, a lifted one and a sharp rim stroke.
Listen as the drum plays a four-beat phrase and the pads light up in order.
Then answer it: strike the same pads in the same rhythm.
Play the three songs in turn; each holds four short phrases.
rules: The drum plays a phrase of four beats, then you answer it, in turn through the song.
A stroke within a hair of the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and a missed one scores nothing.
An extra stroke while you answer costs a few points.
The deep, middle and lifted strokes stand for the gourd sunk, held and raised in the water; the rim stroke is on the edge.
Three stars need roughly nine notes in ten on time.
heritageNote: Water drums are played by women in several Sahel communities of Niger and Nigeria, often in groups with one gourd each in a shared basin. The gourds are cut by hand and the amount of water is adjusted to taste to tune the drum.
